headline: Every trip starts and ends on foot
intro: In Namibia, about one in three people killed on the roads is walking. See the street from behind the wheel, then from the pavement.

contentNotice.text: Some parts talk about the risk of a person on foot being killed or seriously injured. There are no crash images: scenes stop before any contact.

Minibus taxis are pulling in to drop people off. People are crossing between parked cars to reach them.

scenes.title: If a car hits a person walking: their risk of dying
scenes.caption: A small rise in speed sharply raises the risk. The WHO says a person's risk of dying is about {claim:int.who.ped-50-65|value} times higher when hit at {n:65} km/h than at {n:50} km/h.

feedback.green: People step out from between taxis, from busy stalls and onto crossings. Slow down and expect them.
feedback.orange: Some of these you found, some you missed. Taxi stops, stalls and crossings are where people step out.
feedback.red: Look again: taxi stops, stalls and crossings are where people step into the road.

lines: Where people are walking, slow down. Every km/h less shortens your stopping distance.
Expect people to step out from between taxis, parked cars and stalls.
Stop for people on a zebra crossing. In Namibia it's the law, and it's their right of way.

scenes.question: In {n:2021}, what share of people killed on Namibia's roads were pedestrians?

art.alt: A person walking, with symbols for a minibus taxi and the city.

lines: You've just got off a minibus taxi on a busy Windhoek street. The supermarket is on the other side.
There are taxis parked at the stop, stalls on the pavement, and a zebra crossing a little further along.

scenes.prompt: Where will you cross? Tap a point.

art.alt: Top-down view of the street: you're on the left pavement by the taxi stop. A zebra crossing with a refuge island is a short walk up the street. Shaded areas show what parked vehicles hide from you.

points.label: Between the taxis
points.title: Hidden from drivers
points.reason: The taxis block your view of the traffic, and drivers can't see you until you step out. And with a crossing this close, the law expects you to use it.

points.label: At the zebra crossing
points.title: The safest place
points.reason: Drivers must yield to you on the crossing, and the refuge island lets you cross one direction of traffic at a time. Still wait until you're sure cars are stopping.

points.label: By the stalls
points.title: You can see, but…
points.reason: You had a clear view and waited for a gap. But you're less than {claim:na.law.ped-50m} from a crossing, so Namibian law says to cross there instead.

scenes.title: People on foot among those killed on Namibia's roads, {n:2021}
scenes.caption: About {claim:na.stat.ped-share} of people killed on the roads were walking. Early in {n:2025}, {claim:na.stat.ped-deaths-2025} pedestrians died in just over four months, {claim:na.stat.ped-rise-2025} more than a year before.

scenes.explain: {claim:na.stat.ped-share} of people killed on Namibian roads in {n:2021} were pedestrians: about one in three.

steps.title: Use the crossing
steps.body: If there's a pedestrian crossing or an intersection within {claim:na.law.ped-50m}, the law says to cross there.

steps.title: Stop, look and listen
steps.body: Check both ways, and keep looking as you cross. Don't step out until you're sure drivers have seen you and are stopping.

steps.title: Never step out from behind a taxi
steps.body: A stopped taxi or bus hides you from drivers coming past it. Wait until it has gone, or walk to where you can see clearly.

steps.title: Face the traffic
steps.body: Where there's no pavement, walk on the right-hand side of the road, facing oncoming vehicles, so you can see them coming.

steps.title: Be seen at night
steps.body: Wear something light or reflective, and use your phone's torch. Drivers on dipped lights see you much later than you think.

lines: Cross at a crossing or intersection when there's one nearby.
Never assume a driver has seen you. Wait until they stop.
Phone away, eyes up, every time you cross.

scenes.title: The short cut
scenes.label: A made-up story, based on common situations
scenes.warning: This story mentions a pedestrian being hurt. It doesn't describe the injury in detail.
paragraphs: Every afternoon Selma got off the taxi on the busy side of the road. The crossing was only a short walk away, but the short cut between the parked taxis was quicker.
One day a car came past the taxis just as she stepped out. The driver braked, but couldn't stop in time.
Selma's leg was broken and she missed most of her final term at school. 'It was a few seconds saved,' she says. 'It cost me months.'
She walks to the crossing now, and tells her younger brother to do the same.

signpost.text: If a crash has affected you or someone close to you, you don't have to deal with it alone. LifeLine/ChildLine Namibia offers free counselling: call {claim:na.support.lifeline}.
